To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

rat hepatocytes cocultivated overnight in stationary cultures of L517Y/TK+ cells can be used to metabolically activate 7 different procarcinogens, 5 of which were not active in the absence of the hepatocytes.
rat hepatocytes are able to activate a variety of procarcinogenic chemicals to mutagens, including 2-aminofluorene, 2-aminoaanthracene, and N-nitroso compounds, in the L51778Y/TK gene-mutation assay.
rat hepatocytes activated 8 of 10 procarcinogens tested to mutagens in a L5178Y TK gene mutation assay.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an in vitro test for carcinogenesis which can be used to screen chemicals for potential carcinogenicity.
the activation of carcinogens to mutagens.
the use of cultured rat hepatocytes as a source of activating enzymes for the in vitro activation of procarinogens to mutagens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
rat hepatocytes in vitro can activate a variety of procarcinogenic aromatic amines and nitrosamines, and some polycyclic hydrocarbons to mutagens in this assay.
the L5178 Y/TK+/- mutation assay is an excellent system for the detection of mutagenic activity by procarcinogens in the presence of rat hepatocytes.

hepatocytes are capable of metabolizing a variety of procarcinogen compounds, including aromatic amines, nitrosamines, and polycyclic hydrocarbons, to active metabolites that can be mutagenic to the L5178/Y/TK+/- mouse lymphoma assay.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hepatocytes can activate all the compounds we have tested to mutagens, but the degree of activation is highly variable.
hepatocyte-mediated activation in the L517Y/TK mutation test is most effective for aromatic amines, less effective for polycyclic hydrocarbons, and not effective for N-nitrosamines.
hepatocytes are not required for the activation of DPrN, but are essential for activation of aromatic amines and nitrosamines and are not required for activation of polycyclic hydrocarbons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of hepatocytes to activate promutagens in a mammalian cell mutagenesis assay is feasible and may be useful for identifying new mutagens.
hepatocytes can be a useful adjunct to other cell culture assays of procarcinogen mutagenicity.

the presence of hepatocyte coculture is required for the mutagenic activation of most procarcinogens, and that the hepatocyte coculture system can be used to activate procarcinogens in a manner consistent with the known metabolic activation pathways for these compounds.
